sources.entry: Firezone - Secure remote access gateway that supports the WireGuard protocol. It offers a Web GUI, 1-line install script, multi-factor auth (MFA), and SSO. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Elixir/Docker
Firezone | Zero-trust access platform built on WireGuard

summary.one_liner: Firezone is a zero-trust remote access platform built on WireGuard that lets users reach private applications, databases, servers, and subnets through identity-based policies.
summary.what_it_does: Firezone connects users to private resources using WireGuard tunnels, with access granted per group through policies that can require device attestation. Gateways run inside your own infrastructure near the resources they protect, and multiple Gateways can be deployed for load balancing and failover. A Device Pools feature creates a peer-to-peer WireGuard mesh between client devices without a Gateway. The README describes identity provider integration with Google Workspace, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or OIDC, plus directory sync, and audit logs with 90-day retention that can be exported to a SIEM via Log Sinks. Clients are listed for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android, with headless clients for automated workloads. The repo is a monorepo whose elixir/ directory holds the admin portal and control plane, and whose rust/ directory holds the data plane, gateway, relay, and clients.
use_cases: secure remote access to internal servers and databases
routing access to private subnets over WireGuard
group-based access policies with device trust
exporting access audit logs to a SIEM
how_to_run: Cloud: sign up for the managed service and follow the Quickstart to deploy a Gateway, define Resources and policies, then install a Client
Development or evaluation: follow CONTRIBUTING.md to run a local environment
notable: Device Trust using X.509 certificates issued by MDM or enterprise PKI
Device Pools for client-to-client WireGuard mesh without a Gateway
Shared Rust data plane with platform-specific I/O optimizations and published throughput figures
Relays using eBPF/XDP and SR-IOV for traffic when direct connections fail
caveats: Production self-hosting is not officially supported; published Clients are only guaranteed to work with the managed service
Self-hosted portals may require Clients built from a compatible revision
Audit logs have 90-day retention and some features depend on plan tier
